claim: Since the 1960s, a single class of agent has been licensed targeting virus-encoded ion channels, or 'viroporins'.
source: Since the 1960s, a single class of agent has been licensed targeting virus-encoded ion channels, or 'viroporins', contrasting the success of channel blocking drugs in other areas of medicine.
evidence: This is a statement about the historical licensing of viroporin-targeting agents, presented as established fact in the abstract.

claim: Resistance arose to adamantane inhibitors of the influenza A virus (IAV) M2 proton channel.
source: Although resistance arose to these prototypic adamantane inhibitors of the influenza A virus (IAV) M2 proton channel, a growing number of clinically and economically important viruses are now recognised to encode essential viroporins providing potential targets for modern drug discovery.
evidence: This is stated as a known fact about adamantane resistance in the abstract.

claim: A growing number of clinically and economically important viruses encode essential viroporins.
source: Although resistance arose to these prototypic adamantane inhibitors of the influenza A virus (IAV) M2 proton channel, a growing number of clinically and economically important viruses are now recognised to encode essential viroporins providing potential targets for modern drug discovery.
evidence: This is presented as current scientific consensus in the abstract.

claim: The authors describe the first rationally designed viroporin inhibitor with a comprehensive structure-activity relationship (SAR).
source: We describe the first rationally designed viroporin inhibitor with a comprehensive structure-activity relationship (SAR).
evidence: This is a primary claim of the manuscript stated in the abstract.

claim: The rationally designed viroporin inhibitor revealed a second biological function for the p7 viroporin from hepatitis C virus (HCV) during virus entry.
source: This step-change in understanding not only revealed a second biological function for the p7 viroporin from hepatitis C virus (HCV) during virus entry, but also enabled the synthesis of a labelled tool compound that retained biological activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the manuscript stated in the abstract.

claim: The synthesis of a labelled tool compound that retained biological activity was enabled by the comprehensive SAR.
source: This step-change in understanding not only revealed a second biological function for the p7 viroporin from hepatitis C virus (HCV) during virus entry, but also enabled the synthesis of a labelled tool compound that retained biological activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the manuscript stated in the abstract.

claim: p7 inhibitors (p7i) represent a unique class of HCV antiviral targeting both the spread and establishment of infection.
source: Hence, p7 inhibitors (p7i) represent a unique class of HCV antiviral targeting both the spread and establishment of infection, as well as a precedent for future viroporin-targeted drug discovery.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the findings presented in the abstract.

claim: p7 inhibitors set a precedent for future viroporin-targeted drug discovery.
source: Hence, p7 inhibitors (p7i) represent a unique class of HCV antiviral targeting both the spread and establishment of infection, as well as a precedent for future viroporin-targeted drug discovery.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the findings presented in the abstract.

claim: WHO estimates put the total number of deaths due to HCV infection in 2015 at more than 400,000.
source: WHO estimates put the total number of deaths due to HCV infection in 2015 at more than 400 000, with ~1.75 million new infections annually.
evidence: This is a citation of WHO data presented as established fact.

claim: There are approximately 1.75 million new HCV infections annually.
source: WHO estimates put the total number of deaths due to HCV infection in 2015 at more than 400 000, with ~1.75 million new infections annually.
evidence: This is a citation of WHO data presented as established fact.

claim: Current DAA target three proteins within the viral replicase (NS3/4A protease, NS5A and the NS5B RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRP)).
source: Current DAA target three proteins within the viral replicase (NS3/4A protease, NS5A and the NS5B RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRP)), with drug combinations available for treating each of the eight viral genotypes.
evidence: This is stated as current knowledge about DAA targets.

claim: Drug combinations are available for treating each of the eight HCV genotypes.
source: Current DAA target three proteins within the viral replicase (NS3/4A protease, NS5A and the NS5B RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRP)), with drug combinations available for treating each of the eight viral genotypes.
evidence: This is stated as current knowledge about DAA availability.

claim: Resistant viral variants are an increasing concern.
source: Resistant viral variants are an increasing concern (Pawlotsky, 2016), with recent reports of increased resistance amongst some rarer viral subtypes (Fourati et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Recent reports show increased resistance amongst some rarer HCV viral subtypes.
source: Resistant viral variants are an increasing concern (Pawlotsky, 2016), with recent reports of increased resistance amongst some rarer viral subtypes (Fourati et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Fourati et al., 2019.

claim: Recent studies suggest that DAA are less able to reduce the risk of HCC in treated patients compared with IFN-based therapy.
source: Moreover, recent studies suggest that DAA are less able to reduce the risk of HCC in treated patients compared with IFN-based therapy (Baumert and Hoshida, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Baumert and Hoshida, 2019.

claim: DAA-induced reduction in HCC risk may be linked to virus-induced host epigenetic signatures that are not reversed following DAA cure.
source: This may be linked to virus-induced host epigenetic signatures that are not reversed following DAA cure (Hamdane et al., 2019; Perez et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a speculative connection supported by citations.

claim: The 63 amino acid p7 protein is capable of oligomerising (forming hexamers and/or heptamers).
source: Furthermore, the 63 amino acid p7 protein is capable of oligomerising (forming hexamers and/or heptamers Luik et al., 2009; Clarke et al., 2006) within membranes to form an ion channel complex (Breitinger et al., 2016; Premkumar et al., 2004; Pavlović et al., 2003; Griffin et al., 2003) with a distinct, but equally essential role during virion secretion (Steinmann et al., 2007a; Jones et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: p7 oligomers form an ion channel complex within membranes.
source: Furthermore, the 63 amino acid p7 protein is capable of oligomerising (forming hexamers and/or heptamers Luik et al., 2009; Clarke et al., 2006) within membranes to form an ion channel complex (Breitinger et al., 2016; Premkumar et al., 2004; Pavlović et al., 2003; Griffin et al., 2003) with a distinct, but equally essential role during virion secretion (Steinmann et al., 2007a; Jones et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: p7 channel activity comprises the raising of secretory vesicle pH, which is necessary to protect acid-labile intracellular virions.
source: This comprises the raising of secretory vesicle pH, which is necessary to protect acid-labile intracellular virions (Atkins et al., 2014; Bentham et al., 2013; Wozniak et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Adamantanes and alkyl imino-sugars inhibit p7 channel activity as well as virion secretion in culture, but with relatively poor potency.
source: Prototypic compounds, such as adamantanes and alkyl imino-sugars, inhibit p7 channel activity as well as virion secretion in culture, but with relatively poor potency (Griffin et al., 2008; Steinmann et al., 2007b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Leu20Phe confers resistance in genotype 1b and 2a p7 to adamantanes, including rimantadine.
source: This includes Leu20Phe, which confers resistance in genotype 1b and 2a p7 to adamantanes, including rimantadine.
evidence: This is stated as an established finding in the introduction.

claim: The majority of p7 structural studies support the folding of protomers into a hairpin conformation.
source: The majority of p7 structural studies support the folding of protomers into a hairpin conformation (Luik et al., 2009; Foster et al., 2014; Cook et al., 2013; Montserret et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: A solution NMR structure of a complete hexameric p7 channel complex comprised protomers in an unusual intertwined triple-helix configuration (PDB: 2M6X).
source: However, a solution NMR structure of a complete hexameric p7 channel complex comprised protomers in an unusual intertwined triple-helix configuration (PDB: 2M6X) (OuYang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to OuYang et al., 2013.

claim: Recent studies have questioned the validity of the 2M6X structure due to potential artefacts caused by alkyl-phosphocholine detergents used as membrane mimetics.
source: Furthermore, recent studies have questioned the validity of this structure due to potential artefacts caused by alkyl-phosphocholine detergents used as membrane mimetics Oestringer et al., 2018; the original authors contest this notion (Chen et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Molecular dynamics simulations favour the stability and channel gating characteristics of hairpin-based structures.
source: However, molecular dynamics simulations favour the stability and channel gating characteristics of hairpin-based structures (Chandler et al., 2012; Holzmann et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Both hairpin- and triple-helix-based channel structures retain an adamantane-binding site upon the channel periphery that includes position 20.
source: Interestingly, both hairpin- and triple-helix-based channel structures retain an adamantane- binding site upon the channel periphery that includes position 20 (Foster et al., 2014; OuYang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Initial hit compounds from in silico screening displayed considerably improved potency compared with rimantadine that was independent of Leu20Phe mutations.
source: Resultant chemical hits displayed considerably improved potency compared with rimantadine that was independent of Leu20Phe mutations (Foster et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Foster et al., 2014.

claim: The optimised IncuCyte assay has a Z factor of 0.47 ± 0.14.
source: The assay Z factor was determined as 0.47 ± 0.14, with a % coefficient variation of 16.9 ± 4.3 and a signal/background ratio of 81.1 ± 23.6 (data from two independent positive and negative controls (SOF, DCV, DMSO only), in duplicate, averaged over three independent experimental repeats, with three separate assay plates, over two separate days).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the assay validation experiments.

claim: JK3/32 has an EC50 of approximately 184 nM against chimaeric genotype 1b HCV (J4/JFH-1) secretion.
source: SAR-focused chemical modification (Table 1) of an oxindole core scaffold identified 'JK3/32' as a series lead with excellent potency against chimaeric genotype 1b HCV (J4/JFH-1) secretion (EC50 ~184 nM) (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding reported in the results.

claim: JK3/32 retained cross-genotype activity versus HCV genotype 3a (EC50 ~738 nM).
source: As seen for first generation compounds (Foster et al., 2014), JK3/32 retained cross-genotype activity versus HCV genotype 3a (EC50 ~738 nM), with a modest reduction in activity against more genetically distant 2a viruses (EC50 ~1900 nM) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding reported in the results.

claim: JK3/32 showed a modest reduction in activity against genotype 2a viruses (EC50 ~1900 nM).
source: As seen for first generation compounds (Foster et al., 2014), JK3/32 retained cross-genotype activity versus HCV genotype 3a (EC50 ~738 nM), with a modest reduction in activity against more genetically distant 2a viruses (EC50 ~1900 nM) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding reported in the results.

claim: JK3/32 showed a toxicity-based selectivity index of >500 (CC50 >100,000 nM).
source: The compound showed a toxicity-based selectivity index of >500 (CC50 >100 000 nM) based upon confluency (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C) and MTT assay (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) in Huh7 cells, and had no discernible effect upon replication of HCV JFH-1 subgenomic replicons, which retain the same replicase as chimaeric viruses but lack the structural proteins, p7 and NS2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding reported in the results.

claim: JK3/32 had no discernible effect upon replication of HCV JFH-1 subgenomic replicons.
source: The compound showed a toxicity-based selectivity index of >500 (CC50 >100 000 nM) based upon confluency (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C) and MTT assay (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) in Huh7 cells, and had no discernible effect upon replication of HCV JFH-1 subgenomic replicons, which retain the same replicase as chimaeric viruses but lack the structural proteins, p7 and NS2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding reported in the results.

claim: JK3/32 displayed no off-target activity against a panel of human kinases tested commercially.
source: However, the JK series of inhibitors is chemically distinguished from these compounds by an N-alkyl substituent, which was essential for anti-HCV activity (Table 1); accordingly, JK3/32 displayed no off-target activity against a panel of human kinases tested commercially (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding reported in the results.

claim: BIT225 showed no antiviral activity discernible from effects upon cellular viability in the authors' hands.
source: However, in our hands BIT225 showed no antiviral activity discernible from effects upon cellular viability (Figure 1—figure supplement 5); notably, no assessment of cellular toxicity was undertaken during previously reported HCV studies (Meredith et al., 2013), which used a concentration higher (30 μM) than the observed Huh7 CC50 herein (18.6 μM) during short timescale assays (6–24 hr).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding reported in the results.

claim: JK3/32 is predicted to bind into a predominantly hydrophobic cleft created between helices on the membrane-exposed site.
source: JK3/32 is predicted to bind into a predominantly hydrophobic cleft created between helices on the membrane-exposed site (Figure 2a,b).
evidence: This is based on computational docking predictions shown in Figure 2.

claim: Predicted polar interactions occur between the side-chains of Tyr45 and Trp48 and the carbonyl oxygen atom at the indole core of JK3/32.
source: Predicted polar interactions occur between the side-chains of Tyr45 and Trp48 side and the carbonyl oxygen atom at the indole core (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is based on computational docking predictions shown in Figure 2.

claim: The majority of residues within the JK3/32 binding site are highly conserved; all residues are >90% conserved with the exception of Leu20 (45.67%) and Tyr45 (84.67%).
source: Importantly, the majority of residues within this binding site are highly conserved; all residues are >90% conserved with the exception of Leu20 (45.67%) and Tyr45 (84.67%) (Figure 2d, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on sequence conservation analysis shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Unlike rimantadine, Leu20Phe does not mediate resistance to the JK3/32 chemical series.
source: However, unlike rimantadine, Leu20Phe does not mediate resistance to this chemical series (Foster et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Foster et al., 2014.

claim: JK3/32 SAR was consistent with its predicted binding pose following docking within the peripheral binding site.
source: JK3/32 SAR was consistent with its predicted binding pose (Figure 2e and Table 1) following docking within the peripheral binding site, defining key determinants of its activity.
evidence: This is based on comparison of experimental SAR data with computational predictions.

claim: Consistency between observed SAR and the heptameric 3ZD0-based model supports that rational design based upon this system generates authentic, specific p7-targeted antivirals.
source: Consistency between observed SAR and the heptameric 3ZD0-based model supports that rational design based upon this system generates authentic, specific p7-targeted antivirals; JK3/32 SAR was not consistent with the 2M6X structure (data not shown).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the SAR and modeling data.

claim: JK3/32 SAR was not consistent with the 2M6X structure.
source: Consistency between observed SAR and the heptameric 3ZD0-based model supports that rational design based upon this system generates authentic, specific p7-targeted antivirals; JK3/32 SAR was not consistent with the 2M6X structure (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from unpublished data.

claim: Atomistic simulations (100 ns) of JK3/32 bound to the peripheral site revealed marked stability of its binding pose.
source: Encouragingly, atomistic simulations (100 ns) of JK3/32 bound to the peripheral site revealed marked stability of its binding pose, despite significant structural dynamics of the p7 bundle observed in hydrated lipid bilayers (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is based on molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 3.

claim: JK3/32 remained within the binding pocket throughout the course of the 100 ns simulation.
source: JK3/32 remained within the binding pocket throughout the course of the simulation, with the carbonyl group initially forming H-bonds with Tyr45 followed by subsequent bifurcation (after ~50 ns) with Trp48 (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is based on molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Leu20Phe mutant p7 complexes formed a stable interaction with JK3/32.
source: Leu20Phe mutant p7 complexes also formed a stable interaction with JK3/32 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), although Phe20 caused reorganisation and crowding of the binding pocket stabilised by π-π stacking interactions between Phe20 and Tyr45.
evidence: This is based on molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: p7 with the Leu20Phe mutation disrupted binding of rimantadine within the pocket, with the drug failing to make H-bond contacts and leaving the pocket over the course of the simulation.
source: By contrast, p7 with the Leu20Phe mutation disrupted binding of rimantadine within the pocket, with the drug failing to make H-bond contacts and leaving the pocket over the course of the simulation (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: JK3/32 reduced infectivity when added to infectious genotype 1b innoculae.
source: In agreement, JK3/32 reduced infectivity when added to infectious genotype 1b innoculae, but a structurally related analogue lacking activity versus genotype 1b or 3a, compound R21, did not (Figure 4a,b).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4.

claim: Compound R21 did not reduce infectivity when added to infectious genotype 1b innoculae.
source: In agreement, JK3/32 reduced infectivity when added to infectious genotype 1b innoculae, but a structurally related analogue lacking activity versus genotype 1b or 3a, compound R21, did not (Figure 4a,b).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4.

claim: The same genotype-dependent variation in JK3/32 potency was evident during entry experiments as observed during secretion.
source: Reassuringly, the same genotype-dependent variation in JK3/32 potency was evident during entry experiments as observed during secretion; genotype 3a chimaeric viruses required 2–4 fold higher concentration than genotype 1b and R21 again had no effect (Figure 4c).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4.

claim: Entry of genotype 2a JFH-1 HCV is innately amantadine-resistant, yet remains sensitive to rimantadine and the alkyl imino-sugar NN-DNJ.
source: Secretion of genotype 2a JFH-1 HCV is innately amantadine-resistant, yet remains sensitive to rimantadine and the alkyl imino-sugar NN-DNJ. Virus entry experiments recapitulated this pattern, with the latter two compounds displaying dose-dependent efficacy when added to infectious innoculae (Figure 4d).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4.

claim: Entry of JFH-1 Leu20Phe was resistant to both amantadine and rimantadine, whilst remaining NN-DNJ-sensitive.
source: Moreover, entry of JFH-1 Leu20Phe was resistant to both amantadine and rimantadine, whilst remaining NN-DNJ-sensitive; NN-DNJ disrupts p7 oligomerisation rather than binding peripherally (Foster et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding reported in the results.

claim: JK3/32 only blocked infection when introduced during virus infection.
source: Consistently, JK3/32 only blocked infection when introduced during virus infection, concordant with a direct effect upon virion-resident channels, whereas the NS5Ai Daclatasvir only interfered with HCV infection when added post-entry (Figure 4e).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4.

claim: Neither JK3/32 nor R21 added to innoculae had effects upon the entry of pseudotypes possessing patient-derived E1/E2 representing genotype 1b or 3a.
source: Encouragingly, neither JK3/32 nor R21 added to innoculae had effects upon the entry of pseudotypes possessing patient-derived E1/E2 representing genotype 1b or 3a (Urbanowicz et al., 2016a), whereas Galanthus nivalis Agglutinin (GNA) blocked entry in a dose-dependent fashion (Figure 4f).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4.

claim: JK3/32 did not affect IAV entry.
source: Accordingly, JK3/32 did not affect IAV entry (Figure 4g).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4.

claim: JK3/32 did not interfere with clathrin-dependent uptake of fluorescent-tagged epidermal growth factor (EGF).
source: In addition, JK3/32 did not interfere with clathrin-dependent uptake of fluorescent-tagged epidermal growth factor (EGF) (Figure 4h, Figure 4—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4.

claim: The genotype 2a JFH-1 strain displays modest sensitivity to the R21 compound during secretion.
source: Unlike genotypes 1b and 3a, the genotype 2a JFH-1 strain in fact displays modest sensitivity to the R21 compound during secretion (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 5.

claim: R21 blocked JFH-1 entry when added to innoculae.
source: Accordingly, the compound also blocked JFH-1 entry when added to innoculae (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 5.

claim: The Y45T/L50F change in JFH-1 reduced exposure of the R21 molecule to the surrounding environment, permitting a more stable interaction compared to the 1b or 3a channels.
source: Interestingly, the Y45T/L50F change in JFH-1 reduced exposure of the R21 molecule to the surrounding environment, permitting a more stable interaction compared to the 1b or 3a channels; L51C was too distant from R21 to exert any obvious changes in binding.
evidence: This is based on computational modeling analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: Both JK3/32 and JK3/32-488 effectively abrogated infectivity in peak fractions of purified HCV treated with these compounds.
source: However, infectivity was effectively abrogated in peak fractions treated with either JK3/32 or JK3/32-488, although a small number of infected cells were detectable (Figure 7a,b, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 7.

claim: Concentrations of JK3/32-488 within peak infectivity fractions were <2 nM after separation from unbound compound.
source: Quantification of the fluorescent signal from JK3/32-488 revealed concentrations within peak infectivity fractions were <2 nM (fractions 5 and 6).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding reported in the results.

claim: Neither JK3/32 nor JK3/32-488 affected the stability of HCV particles.
source: Importantly, neither JK3/32 nor JK3/32-488 affected the stability of HCV particles as migration of virion-associated core protein corresponded with the peak of infectivity in each case, and was identical to the R21 control (Figure 7d).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 7.

claim: JK3/32 irreversibly blocks virion-resident p7 channels.
source: Hence, we conclude that effects upon HCV entry are not attributable to cellular exposure to JK3/32, and that the compound irreversibly blocks virion-resident p7 channels.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the gradient separation experiments.

claim: Correlation between SAR and channel models constructed using hairpin-shaped protomers supports their biological relevance.
source: First, correlation between SAR and channel models constructed using hairpin-shaped protomers (based upon the 3ZD0 monomeric NMR structure), rather than the 2M6X hexamer, supports their biological relevance.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the SAR and modeling data presented in the discussion.

claim: JK3/32 represents a dramatic leap forward compared with previously described p7i.
source: Our rationally derived lead, JK3/32, and the extensive chemical SAR series that underpins it, represent a dramatic leap forward compared with previously described p7i on several fronts.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the discussion.

claim: JK3/32-based drugs may potentially target two discrete stages of the virus life cycle, namely virion secretion and entry.
source: Moreover, these may potentially target two discrete stages of the virus life cycle, namely virion secretion and entry.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the findings presented in the discussion.

claim: The high degree of conservation within the JK3/32 binding site explains why JK3/32 specific resistance was not selectable in culture.
source: We infer that the high degree of conservation within this site explains why JK3/32 specific resistance was not selectable in culture, despite several attempts.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the conservation data and resistance selection experiments.

claim: The discrete resistance phenotype for the R21 compound supports the relevance of the peripheral binding site.
source: Nevertheless, the discrete resistance phenotype for the R21 compound supports the relevance of the peripheral binding site and provides orthogonal validation that p7 channel activity is required during HCV entry.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the R21 resistance data.

claim: JK3/32 SAR was compatible with 3ZD0-based hairpin-based channel models, but not those based upon the 2M6X channel complex solution structure.
source: It was interesting to note that JK3/32 SAR was compatible with 3ZD0-based hairpin-based channel models, but not those based upon the genotype 5a (EUH1480 isolate) 2M6X channel complex solution structure.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the SAR and modeling data presented in the discussion.

claim: The findings add to the NMR-specific concerns recently raised regarding 2M6X and support that biologically functional p7 channels comprise arrangements of hairpin protomers.
source: Taken together, our findings add to the NMR-specific concerns recently raised regarding 2M6X (Oestringer et al., 2018) and support that biologically functional p7 channels comprise arrangements of hairpin protomers.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the findings presented in the discussion.

claim: BIT225 may show greater potency versus BVDV than HCV.
source: We conclude that BIT225 may show greater potency versus BVDV than HCV, and that selective antiviral effects cannot be determined for HCV in the Huh7 system.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the BIT225 comparison experiments.

claim: Selective antiviral effects of BIT225 cannot be determined for HCV in the Huh7 system.
source: We conclude that BIT225 may show greater potency versus BVDV than HCV, and that selective antiviral effects cannot be determined for HCV in the Huh7 system.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the BIT225 comparison experiments.

claim: The different biological roles of p7 channel activity during secretion and entry may explain why higher p7i concentrations are required to block entry.
source: We speculate that the different biological roles of p7 channel activity during secretion and entry may explain why higher p7i concentrations are required to block the latter process.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation proposed in the discussion.

claim: During secretion, p7 must counteract active proton gradients generated by vATPase in order to prevent acidification within large secretory vesicles, conceivably requiring a considerable number of viroporin complexes.
source: During secretion, p7 must counteract active proton gradients generated by vATPase in order to prevent acidification within large secretory vesicles (Wozniak et al., 2010), conceivably requiring a considerable number of viroporin complexes.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation proposed in the discussion, supported by a citation.

claim: During entry, virion-resident p7 would promote core acidification in the same direction as proton gradients generated within endosomes, presumably achieved by a small number of channel complexes.
source: By contrast, during entry, virion-resident p7 would promote core acidification in the same direction as proton gradients generated within endosomes, presumably achieved by a small number of channel complexes.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation proposed in the discussion.

claim: Basic loop mutations induce defects in p7 stability and E2-p7-NS2 precursor processing within infected cells.
source: Instead, basic loop mutations induce defects in p7 stability and E2-p7-NS2 precursor processing within infected cells (Bentham et al., 2013), as well as severe disruption of membrane insertion observed in vitro (StGelais et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The favourable potency and selectivity index demonstrated by JK3/32 could serve as a high quality starting point for a more comprehensive p7-targeted drug development programme.
source: The favourable potency and selectivity index demonstrated by JK3/32 could serve as a high quality starting point for a more comprehensive p7-targeted drug development programme.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the findings presented in the discussion.

claim: p7i could be ideal for delivering effective antiviral prophylaxis against de novo exposure or transplanted graft re-infection, in addition to use alongside conventional DAA combination therapies treating chronic infection.
source: Hence, p7i could be ideal for delivering effective antiviral prophylaxis against de novo exposure (e.g. needle stick/iatrogenic or perinatal) or transplanted graft re-infection, in addition to use alongside conventional DAA combination therapies treating chronic infection.
evidence: This is a speculative application proposed in the discussion.

claim: Viroporins represent an untapped reservoir of antiviral drug targets that has historically been under-explored following the shortcomings of adamantane M2 inhibitors.
source: In summary, viroporins represent an untapped reservoir of antiviral drug targets that has historically been under-explored following the shortcomings of adamantane M2 inhibitors.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the discussion.

claim: The work shows that it is possible to take a step-change in targeting viroporins, providing a new approach to antiviral therapy and generating novel research tools.
source: Our work shows that it is possible to take a step-change in targeting these proteins, providing a new approach to antiviral therapy and generating novel research tools with which to dissect viroporin function.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the discussion.
